hypotheses.description: The asynchronous order-processing worker pool may be underprovisioned or saturated, causing jobs to queue faster than they are consumed and increasing confirmation latency.
The order-processing queue may be experiencing a downstream dependency slowdown or repeated retries, so messages remain in-flight longer and the backlog grows despite orders being accepted.
A scheduling or consumer-liveness issue may be preventing some order-processing workers from polling the queue or acknowledging tasks, reducing effective throughput and delaying confirmations.

result.root_cause: The order-processing backlog was caused by repeated downstream timeouts in the inventory reservation call, which kept order-worker jobs in-flight longer and triggered retries, slowing completion and increasing queue depth.
result.explanation: Evidence shows the order-processing queue was already heavily backed up while the order-worker was not CPU-saturated, making worker underprovisioning less likely. At the same time, inventory-service latency was high and order-worker logs repeatedly show inventory reservation requests timing out after 5000ms followed by retry attempts. This matches the supported hypothesis that a downstream dependency slowdown and repeated retries were prolonging message handling, causing the backlog and delayed confirmations. There is no evidence that consumer polling or acknowledgment was failing.
